subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “The quality of the mangoes grown in Multan are known across the country.”
o: The quality of the mangoes grown in Multan are known across the country.
The quality of the mangoes grown in Multan is known across the country.
The quality of the mangoes grown in Multan is known across a country.
The quality of the mangoes grown in Multan has been knew across the country.
explanation: The subject is the singular noun “quality”, not “mangoes”, so the verb must be “is”; the other versions add a wrong participle or article.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “We look forward to meet the minister at the ceremony next week.”?
o: We look forward to meeting the minister on the ceremony next week.
We looks forward to meeting the minister at the ceremony next week.
We look forward to meet the minister at the ceremony next week.
We look forward to meeting the minister at the ceremony next week.
explanation: “Look forward to” is followed by a gerund (“meeting”), because “to” here is a preposition; the other options contain an agreement or preposition error.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “This decision should remain between you and I until the board meets.”
o: This decision should remain between you and me until the board meets.
This decision should remain between you and me until the board meet.
This decision should remains between you and me until the board meets.
This decision should remain between you and I until the board meets.
explanation: A preposition (“between”) takes the object pronoun, so “you and me” is correct; the others keep “I” or break agreement.

subject: English
q: The sentence “The course trains officers in reading reports, writing summaries and to deliver briefings.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: The course trained officers in reading reports, writing summaries and delivering briefings since 2010.
The course train officers in reading reports, writing summaries and delivering briefings.
The course trains officers in reading reports, writing summaries and delivering briefings.
The course trains officers in reading reports, writing summaries and to deliver briefings.
explanation: Items in a series should share one form, so “delivering” matches “reading” and “writing”; the other versions break parallelism, agreement or the preposition “trains in”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “Karachi is larger than any city in Pakistan.”
o: Karachi is more larger than any other city in Pakistan.
Karachi is larger than any other city in Pakistan.
Karachi is larger than any city in Pakistan.
Karachi is largest than any other city in Pakistan.
explanation: When a member is compared with the rest of its own group, “other” is needed; the other options use a double or wrong comparative.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “There wasn’t hardly any rain in the district this year.”?
o: There wasn’t hardly any rain in the district this year.
There were hardly any rain in the district this year.
There was hardly any rain in the district this year.
There was hardly any rains in the district this year.
explanation: “Hardly” is already negative, so adding “not” creates a double negative; “rain” here is uncountable and takes “was”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “He has the reputation of being a honest official.”
o: He has the reputation of being an honest official.
He has reputation of being an honest official.
He has the reputation for being an honest officials.
He has the reputation of being a honest official.
explanation: “Honest” begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so it takes “an”; the other options drop the article or mismatch number.

subject: English
q: The sentence “All factories must comply to the new environmental regulations.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: All factories must comply to the new environmental regulations.
All factories must complies with the new environmental regulations.
All factories must comply with the new environmental regulation’s.
All factories must comply with the new environmental regulations.
explanation: The verb “comply” takes the preposition “with”; after the modal “must” the base form is required, and a plural needs no apostrophe.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “She works in the Foreign Office since 2019.”
o: She have worked in the Foreign Office since 2019.
She has worked in the Foreign Office since 2019.
She has worked in the Foreign Office for 2019.
She works in the Foreign Office since 2019.
explanation: An action continuing from a past point to now, marked by “since”, needs the present perfect “has worked”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “After reading the report, the proposal seemed weak to the committee.”?
o: After read the report, the committee found the proposal weak.
After reading the report, the committee finds the proposal weak yesterday.
After reading the report, the proposal seemed weak to the committee.
After reading the report, the committee found the proposal weak.
explanation: The opening phrase must attach to the people who read the report, so “the committee” must be the subject; the others keep the dangling phrase or misuse tense and verb form.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “Neither the minister nor his secretaries was available for comment.”
o: Neither the minister nor his secretaries was available for comment.
Neither the minister or his secretaries were available for comment.
Neither the minister nor his secretaries were available for comment.
Neither of the minister nor his secretaries were available for comment.
explanation: With “neither…nor” the verb agrees with the nearer subject, “secretaries”, so “were” is correct; “neither” pairs with “nor”, not “or”.

subject: English
q: The sentence “If I was in your place, I would accept the offer.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: If I were in your place, I would accept the offer.
If I were in your place, I will accept the offer.
If I was in your place, I would accept the offer.
If I were in your place, I would accepted the offer.
explanation: An unreal present condition uses the subjunctive “were” with “would” + base verb in the main clause.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “Politicians should avoid to make promises they cannot keep.”
o: Politicians should avoid to make promises they cannot keep.
Politicians should avoid making promises they cannot kept.
Politician should avoid making promises they cannot keep.
Politicians should avoid making promises they cannot keep.
explanation: The verb “avoid” is followed by a gerund, not an infinitive; the modal “cannot” takes the base form “keep”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Each of the candidates must submit their own form before Friday.”?
o: Each of the candidate must submit his or her own form before Friday.
Each of the candidates must submits his or her own form before Friday.
Each of the candidates must submit his or her own form before Friday.
Each of the candidates must submit his or hers own form before Friday.
explanation: In formal usage the singular “each” is matched by “his or her”; “must” takes the base verb and “each of” needs a plural noun.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “The climate of Quetta is cooler than Lahore.”
o: The climate of Quetta is more cooler than that of Lahore.
The climate of Quetta is cooler than that of Lahore.
The climate of Quetta is cooler than Lahore.
The climate of Quetta is cooler then that of Lahore.
explanation: Like must be compared with like: the climate of one city with “that of” the other; “more cooler” is a double comparative and “then” is not the comparative word.

subject: English
q: The sentence “The news from the flood-hit areas are encouraging.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: The news from the flood-hit areas is encouraging.
The news from the flood-hit area are encouraging.
The news from the flood-hit areas are encouraging.
The news from the flood-hit areas is encourage.
explanation: “News” is singular in form and meaning, so it takes “is”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “The train already left when we reached the station.”
o: The train had already left when we reach the station yesterday.
The train had already leave when we reached the station.
The train had already left when we reached the station.
The train already left when we reached the station.
explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect, so “had already left” is correct.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Can you tell me where does the commissioner live?”?
o: Can you tell me where the commissioner lives at?
Can you tell me where the commissioner lives?
Can you tell me where does the commissioner live?
Can you tell me where the commissioner live?
explanation: An embedded question uses statement order without “does”, and the singular subject needs “lives”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “Her sister is married with a doctor in Peshawar.”
o: Her sister is married to a doctor in Peshawar.
Her sister is married to doctor in Peshawar.
Her sister are married to a doctor in Peshawar.
Her sister is married with a doctor in Peshawar.
explanation: Standard English says “married to” someone; the other versions break agreement or drop the article.

subject: English
q: The sentence “The reform not only improved revenue but also public confidence.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: The reform not only improved revenue but also public confidence.
The reform improved not only revenue but public confidence also too.
The reform improved not only revenue but also the public confidences.
The reform improved not only revenue but also public confidence.
explanation: “Not only” and “but also” should precede parallel elements; here both are nouns, so “not only” must come after the verb.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “One of the main reasons for the delay were the shortage of staff.”
o: One of the main reasons for the delay was the shortage of staff.
One of the main reason for the delay was the shortage of staff.
One of the main reasons for the delay were the shortage of staff.
One of the main reasons for the delay was the shortage in staffs.
explanation: The subject is “one”, so the verb is singular “was”; “one of” needs a plural noun, and “staff” is not pluralised here.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Himalayas form a natural barrier along the north of the subcontinent.”?
o: The Himalayas forms a natural barrier along the north of the subcontinent.
The Himalayas form a natural barrier along the north of the subcontinent.
The Himalayas form natural barrier along the north of the subcontinent.
Himalayas form a natural barrier along the north of the subcontinent.
explanation: Names of mountain ranges take “the”; the plural name takes “form”, and the singular “barrier” needs “a”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “My brother is taller than me by two inches, though I am older.”
o: My brother are taller than I by two inches, though I am older.
My brother is more taller than I by two inches, though I am older.
My brother is taller than I by two inches, though I am older.
My brother is taller than I by two inches, though I am elder.
explanation: In formal grammar “than” is followed by the subject case (“than I [am]”); “elder” is not used with “than” in this construction.

subject: English
q: The sentence “If it will rain tomorrow, the match will be postponed.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: If it rains tomorrow, the match will postponed.
If it will rain tomorrow, the match will be postponed.
If it rain tomorrow, the match will be postponed.
If it rains tomorrow, the match will be postponed.
explanation: In a first conditional the “if” clause takes the simple present, not “will”; the passive needs “be postponed”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “Please return back the files to the registry by noon.”
o: Please returns the files to the registry by noon.
Please return the files to the registry by noon.
Please return back the files to the registry by noon.
Please return the files at the registry by noon.
explanation: “Return” already means “come or give back”, so “back” is redundant; a thing is returned “to” a place.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Mathematics are a compulsory subject at the matriculation level.”?
o: Mathematics is a compulsory subject at the matriculation level.
Mathematics is compulsory subject at the matriculation level.
Mathematics is a compulsory subject on the matriculation level.
Mathematics are a compulsory subject at the matriculation level.
explanation: Subjects of study ending in -ics, such as “mathematics”, are singular and take “is”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “Her essay is as good if not better than mine.”
o: Her essay is as good as, if not better than, my.
Her essay is as good if not better than mine.
Her essay is as good as, if not more better than, mine.
Her essay is as good as, if not better than, mine.
explanation: The first comparison needs its own “as” (“as good as”), with “if not better than” set off as an aside; “more better” is a double comparative and “my” cannot stand alone.

subject: English
q: The sentence “After years in the secretariat, he is used to work late hours.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: After years in the secretariat, he is use to working late hours.
After years in the secretariat, he are used to working late hours.
After years in the secretariat, he is used to working late hours.
After years in the secretariat, he is used to work late hours.
explanation: “Be used to” (accustomed to) is followed by a gerund because “to” is a preposition.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “The committee have submitted its report to the Prime Minister.”
o: The committee has submitted its report to the Prime Minister.
The committee has submit its report to the Prime Minister.
The committee have submitted its report to the Prime Minister.
The committee has submitted it’s report to the Prime Minister.
explanation: A committee acting as one body is singular, so “has” agrees with “its”; “it’s” means “it is”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Most people in the north prefer tea than coffee.”?
o: Most people in the north prefers tea to coffee.
Most of people in the north prefer tea to coffee.
Most people in the north prefer tea than coffee.
Most people in the north prefer tea to coffee.
explanation: “Prefer” is followed by “to”, not “than”; “most people” is plural and needs no “of”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “He did not went to the office yesterday because of the strike.”
o: He has not gone to the office yesterday because of the strike.
He did not go to the office yesterday because of the strike.
He did not went to the office yesterday because of the strike.
He did not go to the office yesterday because the strike.
explanation: After the auxiliary “did”, the main verb takes the base form; a finished past time like “yesterday” rules out the present perfect.

subject: English
q: The sentence “The new clerk is honest, hardworking and has punctuality.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: The new clerk are honest, hardworking and punctual.
The new clerk is honestly, hardworking and punctual.
The new clerk is honest, hardworking and punctual.
The new clerk is honest, hardworking and has punctuality.
explanation: All three complements should be adjectives: “honest, hardworking and punctual”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “Bread and butter are the usual breakfast in many hostels.”
o: Bread and butter is the usual breakfasts in many hostels.
Bread and butter are the usual breakfast in many hostels.
Bread and butter is usual the breakfast in many hostels.
Bread and butter is the usual breakfast in many hostels.
explanation: When two nouns form a single dish or idea, as in “bread and butter”, the verb is singular.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “She has joined an university in Islamabad as a lecturer.”?
o: She has joined an university in Islamabad as a lecturer.
She have joined a university in Islamabad as a lecturer.
She has joined a university in Islamabad as a lecturer.
She has join a university in Islamabad as a lecturer.
explanation: “University” begins with a consonant sound (“yoo”), so it takes “a”; a single job title after “as” needs “a”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “The officer who we interviewed yesterday has been promoted.”
o: The officer whom we interviewed yesterday have been promoted.
The officer whom we interviewed yesterday has been promoted.
The officer whom we interview yesterday has been promoted.
The officer which we interviewed yesterday has been promoted.
explanation: The relative pronoun is the object of “interviewed”, so formal English uses “whom”; “which” is not used for people.

subject: English
q: The sentence “I cannot find nothing wrong with the revised draft.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: I cannot find anything wrong with the revised draft.
I cannot find anything wrong in revised draft.
I cannot found anything wrong with the revised draft.
I cannot find nothing wrong with the revised draft.
explanation: “Cannot” already negates the clause, so “anything”, not “nothing”, must follow.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “A number of students has applied for the scholarship this year.”
o: A number of student have applied for the scholarship this year.
A number of students have applied to the scholarship this year.
A number of students have applied for the scholarship this year.
A number of students has applied for the scholarship this year.
explanation: “A number of” means “several” and takes a plural verb (whereas “the number of” takes a singular verb); one applies “for” a scholarship.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “There are less cars on the road during Ramazan evenings.”?
o: There is fewer cars on the road during Ramazan evenings.
There are fewer car on the road during Ramazan evenings.
There are less cars on the road during Ramazan evenings.
There are fewer cars on the road during Ramazan evenings.
explanation: Countable plural nouns such as “cars” take “fewer”; “less” is for uncountable quantities.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “I read the newspaper when the lights went out.”
o: I was reading the newspaper when the lights had went out.
I was reading the newspaper when the lights went out.
I was reading the newspaper when the lights go out.
I read the newspaper when the lights went out.
explanation: An action in progress interrupted by a sudden past event takes the past continuous “was reading”.

subject: English
q: The sentence “Although she is senior than him, she reports to the same director.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: Although she is senior to him, she reports to the same director.
Although she is senior to him, she report to the same director.
Although she is senior than him, she reports to the same director.
Although she is more senior to him, she reports to the same director.
explanation: Latin comparatives such as “senior”, “junior” and “superior” take “to”, not “than”, and are not preceded by “more”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “Politics have always been his passion since his student days.”
o: Politics has always been his passions since his student days.
Politics have always been his passion since his student days.
Politics has always been his passion since his student days.
Politics is always his passion since his student days.
explanation: As a field of activity, “politics” is treated as singular, so “has” is correct.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “The advisor suggested him to apply for the scholarship early.”?
o: The advisor suggested that he apply to the scholarship early.
The advisor suggest that he apply for the scholarship early.
The advisor suggested him to apply for the scholarship early.
The advisor suggested that he apply for the scholarship early.
explanation: “Suggest” does not take an object plus infinitive; it takes a “that” clause (or a gerund).

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “While driving to work, my phone rang several times.”
o: While I was driving to work, my phone rang several times.
While I was driving at work, my phone rang several times.
While driving to work, my phone rang several times.
While I was driving to work, my phone rung several times.
explanation: The phone was not driving; giving the clause its own subject (“I was”) removes the dangling modifier.

subject: English
q: The sentence “Everyone in the country have a right to education.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: Every ones in the country has a right to education.
Everyone in the country has a right to education.
Everyone in the country has a right for education.
Everyone in the country have a right to education.
explanation: “Everyone” is singular and takes “has”; the noun “right” is followed by “to”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “Government must do more to help poor in rural areas.”
o: The government must do more to help poor in rural areas.
The government must does more to help the poor in rural areas.
The government must do more to help the poor in rural areas.
The government must do more to help the poors in rural areas.
explanation: An adjective used as a noun for a group (“the poor”) takes “the” and has no plural form.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “By the time the minister arrives, we will finish the presentation.”?
o: By the time the minister arrives, we will have finish the presentation.
By the time the minister arrives, we will have finished the presentation.
By the time the minister arrive, we will have finished the presentation.
By the time the minister will arrive, we will have finished the presentation.
explanation: An action completed before a future point takes the future perfect “will have finished”; a time clause with “by the time” uses the present tense.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “Let you and I review the figures before the meeting.”
o: Let you and me review the figures before the meeting.
Let you and me to review the figures before the meeting.
Let you and I review the figures before the meeting.
Let you and me reviews the figures before the meeting.
explanation: “Let” takes an object, so the pronoun must be “me”.

subject: English
q: The sentence “The cabinet will discuss about the budget on Monday.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: The cabinet will discuss about the budget on Monday.
The cabinet will discuss the budget at Monday.
The cabinet will discusses the budget on Monday.
The cabinet will discuss the budget on Monday.
explanation: “Discuss” is transitive and takes a direct object without “about”; days take “on”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “There is many reasons for the rise in food prices.”
o: There are much reasons for the rise in food prices.
There are many reasons for the rise in food prices.
There is many reasons for the rise in food prices.
There are many reason for the rise in food prices.
explanation: In a “there” sentence the verb agrees with the following noun, “reasons”, so “are” is correct; countable nouns take “many”.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Faiz was one of the best poet of his generation.”?
o: Faiz was one of the most best poets of his generation.
Faiz was one of the best poet of his generation.
Faiz was one of best poets of his generation.
Faiz was one of the best poets of his generation.
explanation: “One of the” is followed by a plural noun; “most best” is a double superlative and a superlative needs “the”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “Delegates can travel either by train or they can fly.”
o: Delegates can travels either by train or by air.
Delegates can travel either by train nor by air.
Delegates can travel either by train or by air.
Delegates can travel either by train or they can fly.
explanation: “Either…or” should join parallel elements (“by train…by air”); “either” pairs with “or”, not “nor”.

subject: English
q: The sentence “It is raining for three days and the rivers are rising.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: It has been raining for three days and the rivers are rising.
It has been raining for three days and the rivers is rising.
It has been raining since three days and the rivers are rising.
It is raining for three days and the rivers are rising.
explanation: An action continuing up to now over a stated period takes the present perfect continuous; a period takes “for”, not “since”.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “The scissors is lying on the tailor’s table.”
o: The scissors is lying on the tailor’s table.
The scissors are lying on the tailors table.
The scissors are laying on the tailor’s table.
The scissors are lying on the tailor’s table.
explanation: “Scissors” is a plural noun and takes “are”; “lie” (not “lay”) means to rest, and the possessive needs an apostrophe.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “If I would have known about the meeting, I would have attended it.”?
o: If I had known about the meeting, I would have attended it.
If I would have known about the meeting, I would have attended it.
If I had known about the meeting, I would attended it.
If I had knew about the meeting, I would have attended it.
explanation: A third conditional uses the past perfect (“had known”) in the “if” clause, not “would have”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “One should always do his duty honestly.”
o: One should always does one’s duty honestly.
One should always do one’s duty honest.
One should always do one’s duty honestly.
One should always do ones duty honestly.
explanation: In formal English the indefinite “one” is followed by “one’s”; “should” takes the base verb and “do” is modified by the adverb “honestly”.

subject: English
q: The sentence “I congratulated her for her success in the CSS examination.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: I congratulate her on her success in the CSS examination yesterday.
I congratulated her on her success in the CSS examination.
I congratulated she on her success in the CSS examination.
I congratulated her for her success in the CSS examination.
explanation: One congratulates a person “on” an achievement.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “All the furnitures in the new office were imported.”
o: All the furniture at new office was imported.
All the furniture in the new office were imported.
All the furniture in the new office was imported.
All the furnitures in the new office were imported.
explanation: “Furniture” is uncountable: it has no plural and takes a singular verb.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “No sooner the speech ended than the audience stood up.”?
o: No sooner had the speech ended than the audience stood up.
No sooner had the speech ended than the audience stand up.
No sooner the speech ended than the audience stood up.
No sooner had the speech ended when the audience stood up.
explanation: A sentence beginning with “no sooner” needs inverted order (“had the speech ended”) and is completed by “than”.

subject: English
q: Select the grammatically correct form of: “Holy Quran was revealed over a period of about twenty-three years.”
o: The Holy Quran was revealed over period of about twenty-three years.
The Holy Quran was revealed over a period of about twenty-three years.
The Holy Quran were revealed over a period of about twenty-three years.
Holy Quran was revealed over a period of about twenty-three years.
explanation: The titles of religious scriptures take the definite article: “the Holy Quran”; the singular noun “period” needs “a”.

subject: English
q: The sentence “When I was a child, we have lived in Hyderabad.” contains an error. Choose its correct form.
o: When I was a child, we have lived in Hyderabad.
When I was a child, we use to live in Hyderabad.
When I was child, we lived in Hyderabad.
When I was a child, we lived in Hyderabad.
explanation: A finished past period (“when I was a child”) takes the simple past, not the present perfect.

subject: English
q: Choose the correct version of the sentence: “It was her who first reported the leak to the engineers.”
o: It was she whom first reported the leak to the engineers.
It was she who first report the leak to the engineers.
It was she which first reported the leak to the engineers.
It was she who first reported the leak to the engineers.
explanation: In formal English the complement of “be” takes the subject case (“It was she”), and the relative pronoun is the subject of “reported”, so “who” is needed; “which” is not used for a person.

subject: English
q: Which of the following is the correct form of “Rice as well as wheat are grown in the plains of Punjab.”?
o: Rice as well as wheat is grown in the plains of Punjab.
Rice as well as wheat is grown in plains of Punjab.
Rice as well as wheat is grow in the plains of Punjab.
Rice as well as wheat are grown in the plains of Punjab.
explanation: A phrase introduced by “as well as” does not change the number of the subject “rice”, so the verb is singular.
